questions.e: HUMID means containing a lot of moisture in the air, i.e. DAMP. HOT is tempting because humid weather is often hot, but heat and moisture are different things; DRY is the opposite.

questions.s: In the sentence "The children were told to be CAUTIOUS while crossing the busy road.", the word CAUTIOUS most nearly means
questions.e: CAUTIOUS means taking care to avoid danger, i.e. CAREFUL, which suits crossing a busy road. CURIOUS (eager to know) only sounds alike.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: CEASE
questions.e: CEASE means to come or bring to an end, i.e. STOP. BEGIN is the opposite, and SEIZE sounds almost the same but means to grab.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: MEND
questions.e: MEND means to put something broken back into good condition, i.e. REPAIR. BREAK is the opposite, and LEND and MIND only look similar.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: COMPLACENT
questions.e: COMPLACENT means too pleased with oneself to see dangers or the need to improve, i.e. SMUG. COMPLIANT looks similar but means willing to obey, and ANXIOUS is close to the opposite.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: DEARTH
questions.e: DEARTH means a lack of something, i.e. a SHORTAGE. PLENTY is the opposite, and DEATH is only a look-alike.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: FEASIBLE
questions.e: FEASIBLE means possible to do easily or practically, i.e. WORKABLE. IMPOSSIBLE is the opposite, and FEEBLE (weak) only shares the first letters.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: SPORADIC
questions.e: SPORADIC means happening now and then, at irregular times, i.e. OCCASIONAL. CONSTANT is the opposite, and ATHLETIC is a trap from the "sport" in the spelling.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: INCESSANT
questions.e: INCESSANT means continuing without a pause, i.e. CONSTANT. INTERMITTENT (stopping and starting) is the opposite, and INNOCENT only sounds similar.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: INEVITABLE
questions.e: INEVITABLE means certain to happen and impossible to avoid, i.e. UNAVOIDABLE. UNLIKELY is close to the opposite, and INVISIBLE only looks similar.

questions.s: In the sentence "The teacher asked Sana to ELABORATE on her idea because the class wanted more details.", the word ELABORATE most nearly means
questions.e: To ELABORATE on something means to give more details, i.e. EXPAND, which fits "wanted more details". COLLABORATE looks alike but means to work together, and SUMMARISE is the opposite.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: NOVICE
questions.e: A NOVICE is a person new to an activity, i.e. a BEGINNER. EXPERT is the opposite, and NOVELIST is a trap from the look-alike word "novel".

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: FEROCIOUS
questions.e: FEROCIOUS means savagely violent, i.e. FIERCE. GENTLE is the opposite, and PRECIOUS only rhymes.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: AUTHENTIC
questions.e: AUTHENTIC means of undisputed origin, real, i.e. GENUINE. IMITATION is the opposite, and ANCIENT is a trap because authentic objects are often old, but age is not authenticity.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: SOLEMN
questions.e: SOLEMN means formal and serious in manner, i.e. SERIOUS. CHEERFUL is the opposite, and SOLAR and SWOLLEN only look or sound similar.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: TRANQUIL
questions.e: TRANQUIL means free from disturbance, i.e. CALM. TURBULENT is the opposite, and TANGIBLE (able to be touched) only shares the opening letters.

questions.s: In the sentence "The new manager tried to PLACATE the angry customers by offering free repairs.", the word PLACATE most nearly means
questions.e: PLACATE means to make someone less angry, i.e. PACIFY, which fits offering free repairs to angry customers. PROVOKE (to make angry) is the opposite, and REPLACE only looks similar.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: UBIQUITOUS
questions.e: UBIQUITOUS means found everywhere, i.e. OMNIPRESENT. RARE is the opposite, and UNIQUE is a trap from the similar start "u-", but it means one of a kind.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: MAGNANIMOUS
questions.e: MAGNANIMOUS means generous and forgiving, especially towards a rival, i.e. GENEROUS. MAGNIFICENT looks alike but means grand or impressive, and PETTY is the opposite.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: SAGACIOUS
questions.e: SAGACIOUS means having good judgement and deep understanding, i.e. WISE. FOOLISH is the opposite, and SARCASTIC and SPACIOUS only share some letters.

questions.s: In the sentence "The doctor assured Ali that the small spot on his skin was INNOCUOUS and needed no treatment.", the word INNOCUOUS most nearly means
questions.e: INNOCUOUS means not harmful, i.e. HARMLESS, which fits "needed no treatment". INAUDIBLE (too quiet to be heard) only shares the prefix, and OFFENSIVE is the opposite.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: ASSIST
questions.e: ASSIST means to give help to someone, i.e. HELP. HINDER (to get in the way) is the opposite, and RESIST only rhymes.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: BRAVE
questions.e: BRAVE means ready to face danger or pain, i.e. COURAGEOUS. COWARDLY is the opposite, and GRAVE only rhymes.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: HUGE
questions.e: HUGE means extremely large, i.e. ENORMOUS. TINY is the opposite, and HUMBLE only shares the opening letters.

questions.s: In the sentence "After the long match, the players were EXHAUSTED and sat down on the grass.", the word EXHAUSTED most nearly means
questions.e: EXHAUSTED means very tired, with no energy left, so TIRED fits players resting after a long match. EXCITED and HUNGRY could also describe players, but neither means drained of energy.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: PERMIT
questions.e: PERMIT means to let someone do something, i.e. ALLOW. FORBID is the opposite, and PERFORM only shares the prefix "per-".

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: SINCERE
questions.e: SINCERE means free from pretence and saying what one truly feels, i.e. HONEST. DECEITFUL is the opposite, and SEVERE only looks similar.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: FAMOUS
questions.e: FAMOUS means known by many people, i.e. RENOWNED. UNKNOWN is the opposite, and FURIOUS only shares the opening letter and ending.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: COURTEOUS
questions.e: COURTEOUS means polite and respectful, i.e. POLITE. RUDE is the opposite, and CURIOUS only sounds similar.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: PROFOUND
questions.e: PROFOUND means very great or showing deep insight, i.e. DEEP ("profound sadness", "a profound thinker"). SHALLOW is the opposite, and PROMINENT (standing out, important) describes visibility, not depth.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: LAMENT
questions.e: LAMENT means to express grief or sorrow, i.e. MOURN. REJOICE is the opposite, and LAMINATE (cover with a thin layer) only looks similar.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: IMPETUOUS
questions.e: IMPETUOUS means acting quickly without thinking, i.e. IMPULSIVE. CAUTIOUS is the opposite, and IMPRESSIVE only shares the prefix "imp-".

questions.s: In the sentence "The scientist's HYPOTHESIS was tested in a series of experiments in Lahore.", the word HYPOTHESIS most nearly means
questions.e: A HYPOTHESIS is an idea suggested as a possible explanation and then tested, i.e. a SUPPOSITION. CONCLUSION is tempting because experiments lead to one, but a conclusion is the result reached after testing, not the idea being tested.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: OMINOUS
questions.e: OMINOUS means suggesting that something bad is going to happen, i.e. THREATENING. PROMISING is the opposite, and ENORMOUS and ANONYMOUS only rhyme.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: VERBOSE
questions.e: VERBOSE means using more words than needed, i.e. WORDY. VERBAL is a trap because it shares the root "verb" (word), but it only means spoken rather than written; CONCISE is the opposite.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: DEFER
questions.e: DEFER means to put off to a later time, i.e. POSTPONE. DIFFER (to be unlike) only sounds similar, and HASTEN (to speed up) is the opposite.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: RUDIMENTARY
questions.e: RUDIMENTARY means involving only the simplest first stages, i.e. BASIC. ADVANCED is the opposite, and RUDE is a trap from the first four letters.

questions.s: In the sentence "Fatima's ANECDOTE about her first day at university made everyone laugh.", the word ANECDOTE most nearly means
questions.e: An ANECDOTE is a short, amusing account of a real event, i.e. a STORY. ANTIDOTE looks alike but is a medicine that counters a poison.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: SPURIOUS
questions.e: SPURIOUS means false or fake though made to look genuine, i.e. BOGUS. AUTHENTIC is the opposite, and CURIOUS only rhymes.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: HINDER
questions.e: HINDER means to make it hard for something to happen, i.e. OBSTRUCT. ENCOURAGE is the opposite, and WANDER only rhymes.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: APATHY
questions.e: APATHY means a lack of interest or concern, i.e. INDIFFERENCE. SYMPATHY shares the root "-pathy" (feeling) but means caring about another's trouble, which is nearly the opposite.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: DISCERN
questions.e: DISCERN means to notice or recognise something not obvious, i.e. PERCEIVE. DISCARD (throw away) only shares the prefix, and IGNORE is the opposite.

questions.s: In the sentence "Critics praised the novel's INTRICATE plot, with its many linked characters.", the word INTRICATE most nearly means
questions.e: INTRICATE means having many detailed, connected parts, i.e. COMPLICATED. INTERESTING is tempting because the critics praised it, but interesting describes appeal, not complexity; SIMPLE is the opposite.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: OBDURATE
questions.e: OBDURATE means stubbornly refusing to change one's mind, i.e. UNYIELDING. DURABLE is a trap from "-durate", but it means long-lasting, and OBEDIENT is nearly the opposite.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: GARRULOUS
questions.e: GARRULOUS means talking a great deal, often about unimportant things, i.e. TALKATIVE. RESERVED (quiet, keeping feelings to oneself) is the opposite, and GALLANT only shares the first letters.

questions.s: In the sentence "Zainab's ENIGMATIC smile left her friends wondering what she was thinking.", the word ENIGMATIC most nearly means
questions.e: ENIGMATIC means difficult to understand or interpret, i.e. MYSTERIOUS, which fits friends wondering what she meant. CHARMING is tempting for a smile, but it means pleasant and attractive, not puzzling.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: CONCEAL
questions.e: CONCEAL means to keep something from being seen or known, i.e. HIDE. REVEAL is the opposite, and CANCEL only shares some letters.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: GLOOMY
questions.e: GLOOMY means dark and depressing, or sad, i.e. DISMAL. CHEERFUL is the opposite, and GLOSSY (shiny) only looks similar.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: PURCHASE
questions.e: PURCHASE means to get something by paying for it, i.e. BUY. SELL is the opposite, and PURSUE (to chase) only shares the first letters.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: ACCURATE
questions.e: ACCURATE means correct in every detail, i.e. EXACT. FAULTY is the opposite, and ADEQUATE (good enough) is a look-alike that describes quantity or quality, not correctness.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: FORTUNATE
questions.e: FORTUNATE means having good luck, i.e. LUCKY. WEALTHY is tempting because "fortune" can mean riches, but a fortunate person need not be rich; UNLUCKY is the opposite.

questions.s: In the sentence "Please do not DISTURB your sister while she is studying.", the word DISTURB most nearly means
questions.e: To DISTURB someone means to interrupt or annoy them, i.e. BOTHER. DISTRUST (to doubt) only shares the prefix "dis-", and HELP does not fit the meaning.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: COMMENCE
questions.e: COMMENCE means to start, i.e. BEGIN. CONCLUDE is the opposite, and COMMENT and COMMEND (praise) only look similar.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: WEARY
questions.e: WEARY means very tired, i.e. FATIGUED. WARY looks alike but means cautious, and FRESH is the opposite.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: CONTEMPT
questions.e: CONTEMPT means the feeling that someone is worthless, i.e. SCORN. RESPECT is the opposite, and CONTENTMENT (satisfaction) only looks similar.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: METHODICAL
questions.e: METHODICAL means done in an orderly, step-by-step way, i.e. SYSTEMATIC. HAPHAZARD (without order) is the opposite, and MEDICAL only looks similar.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: CONCUR
questions.e: CONCUR means to have the same opinion, i.e. AGREE. OBJECT is the opposite, and OCCUR (to happen) and CONQUER only sound similar.

questions.s: In the sentence "The tour guide gave the visitors an ACCOUNT of the history of Lahore Fort.", the word ACCOUNT most nearly means
questions.e: Here ACCOUNT means a spoken or written report of events, i.e. a DESCRIPTION of the fort's history. BILL and DEPOSIT belong to other senses of "account" (money owed, a bank account) that do not fit a tour guide's talk.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: EMULATE
questions.e: EMULATE means to copy someone one admires in order to match them, i.e. IMITATE. EMIGRATE (leave one's country) only looks similar, and IGNORE is the opposite of following an example.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: PROLIFIC
questions.e: PROLIFIC means producing a great deal, e.g. a prolific writer, i.e. PRODUCTIVE. PROFICIENT looks alike but means skilled; a writer can be skilled yet write little. BARREN is the opposite.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: RETICENT
questions.e: RETICENT means not revealing one's thoughts or feelings readily, i.e. RESERVED. OUTSPOKEN is the opposite, and RECENT only looks similar.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: TEDIOUS
questions.e: TEDIOUS means too long, slow or dull, i.e. BORING. EXCITING is the opposite, and STUDIOUS only rhymes.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: BOLSTER
questions.e: BOLSTER means to support or make stronger, i.e. STRENGTHEN ("bolster confidence"). WEAKEN is the opposite, and BOAST only shares the opening letters.

questions.s: In the sentence "Many old buildings in Peshawar were RENOVATED for the tourists.", the word RENOVATED most nearly means
questions.e: RENOVATED means repaired and returned to good condition, i.e. RESTORED. DEMOLISHED (knocked down) is the opposite, and RENAMED only shares the prefix "re-".

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: VINDICATE
questions.e: VINDICATE means to clear someone of blame or suspicion, i.e. EXONERATE. AVENGE is a trap from the look-alike "vindictive" (wanting revenge), and ACCUSE is the opposite.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: SUPERFLUOUS
questions.e: SUPERFLUOUS means more than is needed, i.e. UNNECESSARY. ESSENTIAL is the opposite, and SUPERIOR only shares the prefix "super-".

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: IMPLACABLE
questions.e: IMPLACABLE means unable to be calmed or stopped, i.e. RELENTLESS ("an implacable enemy"). FORGIVING is the opposite, and CAPABLE is a trap from the ending "-able".

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: ASSIDUOUS
questions.e: ASSIDUOUS means showing great care and steady effort, i.e. INDUSTRIOUS. NEGLIGENT is the opposite, and ASSERTIVE (confident and forceful) only shares the first letters.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: TRUCULENT
questions.e: TRUCULENT means eager to argue or fight, i.e. COMBATIVE. TIMID is the opposite, and SUCCULENT (juicy) only rhymes.

questions.s: In the sentence "The judge dismissed the case because the evidence was TENUOUS.", the word TENUOUS most nearly means
questions.e: TENUOUS means very weak or slight, i.e. FLIMSY, which is why the case was dismissed. TEDIOUS (boring) only looks alike, and CONCLUSIVE is the opposite.

questions.s: In the sentence "The flood waters began to RECEDE after three days of sunshine.", the word RECEDE most nearly means
questions.e: RECEDE means to move back or go down from a high level, i.e. SUBSIDE. PROCEED shares the "-ceed/-cede" ending but means to go forward, and RISE is the opposite.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: TRANSPARENT
questions.e: TRANSPARENT means allowing light through so that objects behind can be seen, i.e. SEE-THROUGH. OPAQUE is the opposite, and TEMPORARY only shares the first letter.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: PREDICT
questions.e: PREDICT means to say what will happen in the future, i.e. FORETELL. PROTECT and PREFER only share the prefix "pr-", and FORGET is a look-alike of "foretell".

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: ANNUAL
questions.e: ANNUAL means happening once every year, i.e. YEARLY. DAILY names a different period, and MANUAL (done by hand) only rhymes.

questions.s: In the sentence "The shopkeeper was very GENEROUS and gave the poor family free bread.", the word GENEROUS most nearly means
questions.e: GENEROUS means willing to give freely, i.e. CHARITABLE, which fits giving free bread. GENUINE only shares the first letters, and SELFISH is the opposite.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: ENQUIRE
questions.e: ENQUIRE means to ask for information, i.e. ASK. ANSWER is the opposite, and ACQUIRE (to get) only rhymes.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: PERILOUS
questions.e: PERILOUS means full of danger, i.e. DANGEROUS. SAFE is the opposite, and PERPETUAL (lasting for ever) only shares the prefix "per-".

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: INFER
questions.e: INFER means to reach a conclusion from evidence, i.e. DEDUCE. IMPLY is the classic confusion: the speaker implies (suggests) something, while the listener infers it.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: SCRUPULOUS
questions.e: SCRUPULOUS means very careful to do what is right and correct, i.e. CONSCIENTIOUS. UNPRINCIPLED is the opposite, and SUSPICIOUS only shares the ending "-ous".

questions.s: In the sentence "The committee decided to ABOLISH the outdated rule.", the word ABOLISH most nearly means
questions.e: To ABOLISH a rule means to end it officially, i.e. ELIMINATE it. INTRODUCE is the opposite, and PUBLISH only rhymes; publishing a rule makes it known, not ended.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: CAPRICIOUS
questions.e: CAPRICIOUS means changing mood or behaviour suddenly, i.e. FICKLE. CAPACIOUS looks alike but means roomy, and STEADY is the opposite.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: PLACID
questions.e: PLACID means calm and not easily upset, i.e. SERENE. AGITATED is the opposite, and PALLID (pale) only rhymes.

questions.s: In the sentence "The cricket team's victory BUOYED the spirits of the whole city.", the word BUOYED most nearly means
questions.e: To BUOY spirits means to keep them high, i.e. LIFTED, as a buoy floats on water. DAMPENED is the opposite, and BOUGHT only sounds a little like "buoyed".

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: EQUANIMITY
questions.e: EQUANIMITY means calmness of mind, especially under stress, i.e. COMPOSURE. EQUALITY is a trap from the shared root "equa-", and ANIMOSITY (strong dislike) only shares the ending.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: PARSIMONIOUS
questions.e: PARSIMONIOUS means extremely unwilling to spend money, i.e. MISERLY. EXTRAVAGANT (spending too much) is the opposite, and HARMONIOUS only shares the ending "-monious".

questions.s: In the sentence "Ali's argument was so COGENT that the whole panel accepted it.", the word COGENT most nearly means
questions.e: COGENT means clear, logical and persuasive, i.e. CONVINCING, which explains why the panel accepted it. CUNNING (clever in a deceitful way) is tempting for a clever argument, but it implies trickery, not sound reasoning.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: ANXIOUS
questions.e: ANXIOUS means feeling uneasy about something uncertain, i.e. WORRIED. RELAXED is the opposite, and ENVIOUS (jealous) only shares the ending "-ious".

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: INTERIOR
questions.e: INTERIOR means the inner part of something, i.e. the INSIDE. EXTERIOR is the opposite, and INFERIOR (lower in quality) only looks similar.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: OBTAIN
questions.e: OBTAIN means to get possession of something, i.e. ACQUIRE. LOSE is the opposite, and CONTAIN (to hold inside) only rhymes.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: VICTORY
questions.e: VICTORY means winning a contest or fight, i.e. TRIUMPH. BATTLE is tempting because victories follow battles, but a battle is the fight itself, which can be won or lost; DEFEAT is the opposite.

questions.s: In the sentence "The traveller was ASTONISHED to see snow in Karachi.", the word ASTONISHED most nearly means
questions.e: ASTONISHED means greatly surprised, i.e. AMAZED, which suits the rare sight of snow in Karachi. ASHAMED (feeling guilty) only shares the first letters.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: COMPREHEND
questions.e: COMPREHEND means to grasp the meaning of something, i.e. UNDERSTAND. CONFUSE is close to the opposite, and COMPRESS only shares the prefix "com-".

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: FUTILE
questions.e: FUTILE means producing no useful result, i.e. USELESS. FERTILE only rhymes, FUTURISTIC is a look-alike, and EFFECTIVE is the opposite.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: CORDIAL
questions.e: CORDIAL means warm and friendly, i.e. GENIAL ("a cordial welcome"). FROSTY (cold and unfriendly) is the opposite, and CORAL only looks similar.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: MEAGRE
questions.e: MEAGRE means lacking in quantity or quality, i.e. SCANTY ("a meagre meal"). AMPLE (more than enough) is the opposite, and EAGER is hidden inside the spelling but means keen.

questions.s: In the sentence "Bilal's sudden resignation BAFFLED his colleagues, who had no idea why he left.", the word BAFFLED most nearly means
questions.e: BAFFLED means totally confused, i.e. PUZZLED, which matches "had no idea why". ANGERED is a possible reaction to a resignation but means made angry, not confused.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: HAMPER
questions.e: HAMPER (as a verb) means to slow down or prevent progress, i.e. IMPEDE. PAMPER (to spoil with care) only rhymes, and ASSIST is the opposite.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: VERSATILE
questions.e: VERSATILE means able to adapt to many different uses or tasks, i.e. ADAPTABLE. VOLATILE looks alike but means liable to change suddenly, and LIMITED is the opposite.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: DEPLETE
questions.e: DEPLETE means to use up a supply, i.e. DRAIN ("deplete the water reserves"). REPLENISH (refill) is the opposite, and DELETE (remove text) only looks similar.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: PERNICIOUS
questions.e: PERNICIOUS means having a harmful effect, often gradually, i.e. HARMFUL. BENEFICIAL is the opposite, and SUSPICIOUS only shares the ending "-cious".

questions.s: In the sentence "The old professor's DIDACTIC stories always ended with a moral lesson.", the word DIDACTIC most nearly means
questions.e: DIDACTIC means intended to teach, especially a moral lesson, i.e. INSTRUCTIVE. ENTERTAINING is tempting for stories, but it means amusing, and a story can entertain without teaching; DICTATORIAL only looks similar.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: GIGANTIC
questions.e: GIGANTIC means extremely large, i.e. HUGE. MINUTE (pronounced "my-NEWT") means extremely small, the opposite, and MAGIC only shares some letters.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: GLEAM
questions.e: GLEAM means to give out a soft, bright light, i.e. SHINE. FADE is close to the opposite, and GLEAN (to gather bit by bit) only looks similar.

questions.s: In the sentence "The teacher was PLEASED with Sana's neat homework.", the word PLEASED most nearly means
questions.e: PLEASED means happy with something, i.e. SATISFIED, as a teacher is with neat work. SURPRISED is a possible reaction but means taken unawares, not happy; ANNOYED is the opposite.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: BLATANT
questions.e: BLATANT means done openly and without shame, very obvious ("a blatant lie"), i.e. OBVIOUS. SUBTLE is the opposite, and BLUNT (direct in speech) only looks similar.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: ADEPT
questions.e: ADEPT means very skilled at something, i.e. SKILFUL. CLUMSY is the opposite, and ADOPTED is a look-alike of "adopt", a different word.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: TREPIDATION
questions.e: TREPIDATION means fear or worry about what may happen, i.e. APPREHENSION. CONFIDENCE is the opposite, and IRRITATION (annoyance) only shares the ending "-ation".

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: COHERENT
questions.e: COHERENT means clear and consistent, with parts that fit together, i.e. LOGICAL. INHERENT (existing as a natural part) only rhymes, and MUDDLED is the opposite.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: FRIVOLOUS
questions.e: FRIVOLOUS means not serious, light-minded, i.e. SILLY. SOLEMN is the opposite, and FRIGID (very cold) only shares the first letters.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: DISPARITY
questions.e: DISPARITY means a great difference, i.e. INEQUALITY ("the disparity between rich and poor"). SIMILARITY is the opposite, and DESPAIR and DISPUTE only look similar.

questions.s: In the sentence "The heavy rain made the narrow mountain road TREACHEROUS for drivers.", the word TREACHEROUS most nearly means
questions.e: Here TREACHEROUS means full of hidden dangers, i.e. HAZARDOUS. MUDDY is tempting after heavy rain, but it only means covered in mud; the sentence stresses danger to drivers.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: VENERATE
questions.e: VENERATE means to regard with great respect, i.e. REVERE. DESPISE is the opposite, and VENTILATE and GENERATE only look or sound similar.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: OSTENTATIOUS
questions.e: OSTENTATIOUS means designed to impress or attract notice, i.e. SHOWY. OSTENSIBLE looks alike but means apparent or stated, and MODEST is the opposite.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: EXACERBATE
questions.e: EXACERBATE means to make a problem or pain worse, i.e. AGGRAVATE. EXAGGERATE looks alike but means to overstate, and EASE is the opposite.

questions.s: In the sentence "Feeling CONTRITE after the quarrel, Ayesha apologised to everyone.", the word CONTRITE most nearly means
questions.e: CONTRITE means feeling sorry for having done wrong, i.e. REMORSEFUL, which fits her apology. CONTENTED (satisfied) only shares the prefix "con-", and DEFIANT is the opposite.

questions.s: Choose the word closest in meaning to: INSIPID
questions.e: INSIPID means lacking flavour or interest, i.e. BLAND. INTREPID (fearless) only rhymes, and FLAVOURFUL is the opposite.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: ACCEPT
questions.e: To ACCEPT is to agree to take something offered; to REJECT is to refuse it, so it is the opposite. RECEIVE means much the same as accept, and EXCEPT (to leave out) only sounds like the target.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: GRATITUDE
questions.e: GRATITUDE is the feeling of being thankful; INGRATITUDE is the lack of thanks for kindness received, its direct opposite. THANKFULNESS is a synonym, while GRATUITY (a tip) and LATITUDE (freedom or a map line) merely look similar.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: ARRIVE
questions.e: To ARRIVE is to reach a place; to DEPART is to leave it. REACH is a synonym of the target, and DERIVE (to obtain from a source) is only a look-alike.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: AFFLUENT
questions.e: AFFLUENT means rich and well-off; IMPOVERISHED means made very poor, so it is the opposite. WEALTHY means the same as affluent, and FLUENT and EFFLUENT (liquid waste) only share its spelling.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: ZENITH
questions.e: ZENITH is the highest point of something; NADIR is the lowest point, its exact opposite. SUMMIT is a synonym, HORIZON is the line where earth meets sky, and ZEALOT (a fanatic) only shares the first letters.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: AMATEUR
questions.e: An AMATEUR does something for pleasure, not as a paid job; a PROFESSIONAL does it as a trained, paid occupation. NOVICE (a beginner) and ENTHUSIAST are close in meaning to amateur, and ARMATURE is only a look-alike word.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: INHALE
questions.e: To INHALE is to breathe air in; to EXHALE is to breathe air out, the opposite. BREATHE is close in meaning, and INHABIT (to live in) only shares the first letters.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: ARROGANT
questions.e: ARROGANT means having an exaggerated sense of one's own importance; MODEST means not boastful about one's abilities, its opposite. HAUGHTY is a synonym, and IGNORANT (lacking knowledge) describes a different quality altogether.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: QUELL
questions.e: To QUELL is to put an end to unrest or a rebellion, usually by force; to INCITE is to stir it up, the opposite. SUPPRESS means the same as quell, and QUILL (a feather pen) and QUEST (a search) only look similar.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: IGNITE
questions.e: To IGNITE is to set something on fire; to EXTINGUISH is to put a fire out, the opposite. KINDLE is a synonym, and IGNORE only shares the first letters.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: EXPAND
questions.e: To EXPAND is to become larger; to CONTRACT is to become smaller, as metals do when cooled. EXTEND is close to the target in meaning, and EXPEND (to spend) is a common look-alike trap.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: CONDEMN
questions.e: To CONDEMN is to express strong disapproval of something; to APPLAUD is to praise and approve of it. DENOUNCE means the same as condemn, while CONTEND (to argue) and COMMENT are neutral and not opposites.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: DETERIORATE
questions.e: To DETERIORATE is to become progressively worse; to IMPROVE is to become better. WORSEN is a synonym, and DETERMINE and DECORATE only share the opening letters.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: EXONERATE
questions.e: To EXONERATE is to declare someone free from blame; to INCRIMINATE is to make someone appear guilty, its opposite. ABSOLVE is a synonym, and EXAGGERATE and EXHILARATE (to make very happy) only look similar.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: FREQUENT
questions.e: FREQUENT means happening often; RARE means happening seldom, the opposite. REGULAR is close in meaning to frequent, and FRANTIC (wildly anxious) and RECENT (lately) do not oppose it.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: EXPLICIT
questions.e: EXPLICIT means stated clearly and directly; IMPLICIT means suggested but not stated directly, its opposite. DEFINITE is near in meaning to explicit, and EXPLOIT and ELICIT (to draw out) are look-alikes.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: FICTION
questions.e: FICTION is something invented or imaginary; FACT is something known to be true, the opposite. A FABLE is itself a made-up story, and FRICTION and FUNCTION only rhyme with the target.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: MAXIMUM
questions.e: MAXIMUM is the greatest possible amount; MINIMUM is the smallest possible amount. PEAK is a synonym, and AVERAGE lies between the two extremes rather than opposite one of them.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: CONFIDENT
questions.e: CONFIDENT means sure of oneself; DIFFIDENT means shy and lacking self-confidence, its opposite. SELF-ASSURED is a synonym, and CONFIDENTIAL (meant to be kept secret) is a look-alike trap.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: HARMONY
questions.e: HARMONY is a state of agreement or pleasing combination; DISCORD is disagreement or a clash of sounds, its opposite. ACCORD is a synonym, and MELODY is a related musical word, not an opposite.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: SUPERIOR
questions.e: SUPERIOR means higher in rank or quality; INFERIOR means lower in rank or quality. EXCELLENT is close to superior in meaning, and INTERIOR (inside) is a look-alike that is easily confused with inferior.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: LIBERATE
questions.e: To LIBERATE is to set someone free; to IMPRISON is to lock someone up, the opposite. FREE is a synonym of liberate, and LITERATE (able to read) only looks similar.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: OBFUSCATE
questions.e: To OBFUSCATE is to make something deliberately unclear or confusing; to CLARIFY is to make it clear and easy to understand, the opposite. CONFUSE is a synonym, and SUFFOCATE only rhymes with the target.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: VISIBLE
questions.e: VISIBLE means able to be seen; HIDDEN means kept out of sight, the opposite. APPARENT can mean clearly visible, so it is near in meaning, while VIVID and VALUABLE are unrelated.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: MAGNIFY
questions.e: To MAGNIFY is to make something appear larger; to DIMINISH is to make it smaller. ENLARGE is a synonym, and MAGNETISE and MODIFY (to change) are look-alikes, not opposites.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: OBEDIENT
questions.e: OBEDIENT means willing to follow orders or rules; DEFIANT means openly refusing to obey, its opposite. DUTIFUL is a synonym, and OBVIOUS only shares the first letters.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: BOLD
questions.e: BOLD means brave and willing to take risks; TIMID means shy and easily frightened, the opposite. DARING is a synonym, and BALD only looks like the target.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: PROHIBIT
questions.e: To PROHIBIT is to forbid something officially; to PERMIT is to allow it, the opposite. FORBID is a synonym, and EXHIBIT (to display) only rhymes with the target.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: ACRIMONIOUS
questions.e: ACRIMONIOUS means angry and bitter, as in a quarrel; AMICABLE means friendly and without ill feeling, its opposite. BITTER is a synonym, and CEREMONIOUS (formal) only sounds similar.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: ADVERSARY
questions.e: An ADVERSARY is an enemy or opponent; an ALLY is a supporter on the same side, the opposite. OPPONENT is a synonym, and ADVERSITY (hardship) is a look-alike that means something different.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: ASCEND
questions.e: To ASCEND is to go up; to DESCEND is to go down, the opposite. CLIMB is a synonym, and ASSENT (to agree) only sounds like the target.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: BIGOTED
questions.e: BIGOTED means intolerant of people with different opinions or backgrounds; TOLERANT means accepting of such differences, its opposite. PREJUDICED is a synonym, and IGNORANT (lacking knowledge) is a different idea.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: DORMANT
questions.e: DORMANT means temporarily inactive, as a sleeping volcano is; ACTIVE is its opposite. INACTIVE is a synonym, and DOMINANT (most powerful) is a look-alike trap.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: EXTERNAL
questions.e: EXTERNAL means on the outside; INTERNAL means on the inside, the opposite. OUTER is a synonym, and ETERNAL (lasting for ever) only rhymes with the target.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: DISPARAGE
questions.e: To DISPARAGE is to speak of something as having little worth; to EXTOL is to praise it highly, the opposite. BELITTLE is a synonym, and DISPARATE (very different) is a look-alike adjective.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: ELOQUENT
questions.e: ELOQUENT means fluent and persuasive in speaking; INARTICULATE means unable to express ideas clearly, its opposite. FLUENT is close in meaning to eloquent, and ELEGANT (graceful) only sounds similar.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: FOREIGN
questions.e: FOREIGN means belonging to another country; NATIVE means belonging to a place by birth, the opposite. ALIEN is a synonym, and DISTANT (far away) is a related but different idea.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: EXTRAVAGANT
questions.e: EXTRAVAGANT means spending much more than is necessary; THRIFTY means careful with money, the opposite. LAVISH is a synonym, and EXTRANEOUS (irrelevant) only looks similar.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: IMMENSE
questions.e: IMMENSE means extremely large; TINY means extremely small, the opposite. HUGE is a synonym, and INTENSE (very strong) and IMMERSE (to dip in liquid) only look alike.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: IMPECCABLE
questions.e: IMPECCABLE means without any fault or mistake; FLAWED means having faults, its opposite. FAULTLESS is a synonym, and IMPEACHABLE (able to be charged with wrongdoing) is a look-alike.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: GUILTY
questions.e: GUILTY means responsible for a crime or wrong; INNOCENT means not guilty of it, the opposite. CULPABLE is a synonym meaning deserving blame.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: JUBILANT
questions.e: JUBILANT means feeling great happiness and triumph; DEJECTED means sad and depressed, its opposite. JOYFUL is a synonym, and JUDICIOUS (showing good judgement) only shares the first letters.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: LENIENT
questions.e: LENIENT means mild and tolerant in punishing; STRICT means demanding that rules are obeyed exactly, the opposite. MERCIFUL is a synonym, and LATENT (hidden) and SALIENT (most noticeable) are look-alikes.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: OPTIMIST
questions.e: An OPTIMIST expects good things to happen; a PESSIMIST expects the worst, the opposite. An IDEALIST is close in outlook to an optimist, and OPTICIAN only shares the first letters.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: INDOLENT
questions.e: INDOLENT means lazy and avoiding work; INDUSTRIOUS means hard-working, its opposite. LAZY is a synonym, and INSOLENT (rude and disrespectful) is a look-alike trap.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: MALICIOUS
questions.e: MALICIOUS means intending to harm others; BENIGN means kindly and gentle, the opposite. SPITEFUL is a synonym, and MALLEABLE (easily shaped) only looks similar.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: PERMANENT
questions.e: PERMANENT means lasting for ever or for a very long time; TEMPORARY means lasting only a short time, the opposite. LASTING is a synonym, and PERTINENT (relevant) only sounds similar.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: NOTORIOUS
questions.e: NOTORIOUS means famous for something bad; REPUTABLE means having a good reputation, the opposite. INFAMOUS is a synonym, and NOTABLE (worth noticing) lacks the bad sense but is not its opposite.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: CENSURE
questions.e: To CENSURE is to criticise someone formally and severely; to COMMEND is to praise formally, the opposite. REBUKE is a synonym, and CENSOR (to cut out objectionable material) is a look-alike trap.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: OPAQUE
questions.e: OPAQUE means not letting light through, so one cannot see through it; TRANSPARENT means clear enough to see through, the opposite. CLOUDY is close to opaque, and OBLIQUE (slanting) only looks similar.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: SHALLOW
questions.e: SHALLOW means having little depth; DEEP means extending far down, the opposite. SUPERFICIAL is a synonym when used of thought or wounds, and NARROW refers to width, not depth.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: SPARSE
questions.e: SPARSE means thinly scattered, with few items spread over an area; DENSE means closely packed together, the opposite. SCANTY is a synonym, and SPARE (extra) only looks like the target.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: WANE
questions.e: To WANE is to decrease gradually, as the moon does after full moon; to WAX is to grow larger, the opposite. FADE is a synonym, and WAKE and WADE only differ by one letter.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: TAME
questions.e: TAME describes an animal used to living with people; WILD describes one living in nature without human control, the opposite. DOCILE (gentle and easy to control) is a synonym, and LAME only rhymes with the target.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: MITIGATE
questions.e: To MITIGATE is to make something less severe; to INTENSIFY is to make it stronger or more severe, the opposite. LESSEN is a synonym, and MILITATE (to work against) is a commonly confused look-alike.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: ABSTAIN
questions.e: To ABSTAIN is to choose not to do or have something; to INDULGE is to allow oneself to enjoy it freely, the opposite. REFRAIN is a synonym, and ABSTRACT and OBTAIN only look similar.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: MAJORITY
questions.e: The MAJORITY is the greater number or part; the MINORITY is the smaller number or part, the opposite. BULK is a synonym, and MATURITY (being fully grown) only sounds similar.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: BANISH
questions.e: To BANISH is to send someone away from a place as a punishment; to WELCOME is to receive someone gladly, the opposite. EXPEL is a synonym, and VANISH (to disappear) and PUNISH only rhyme with the target.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: CAPTIVITY
questions.e: CAPTIVITY is the state of being imprisoned or confined; FREEDOM is the state of being free, the opposite. IMPRISONMENT is a synonym, and CAPACITY (the amount something holds) is a look-alike.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: NONCHALANT
questions.e: NONCHALANT means calm and relaxed, showing no worry; ANXIOUS means worried and uneasy, the opposite. CASUAL is a synonym, and NOMINAL (in name only) only shares the first letters.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: COWARD
questions.e: A COWARD is a person who lacks courage; a HERO is admired for courage, the opposite. A WEAKLING is close in meaning, and a TRAITOR betrays others, which is a different fault rather than the opposite.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: DIVERGE
questions.e: To DIVERGE is to move apart in different directions, as two roads may; to CONVERGE is to come together at a point, the opposite. SEPARATE is near in meaning, and DIVERSE (varied) only looks similar.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: FLIMSY
questions.e: FLIMSY means weak and easily damaged; STURDY means strongly built, the opposite. FRAIL is a synonym, and FLASHY (showy) only shares the first letters.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: FLEXIBLE
questions.e: FLEXIBLE means able to bend easily without breaking; RIGID means stiff and unable to bend, the opposite. PLIABLE is a synonym, and FEASIBLE (possible) only rhymes with the target.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: PRODIGAL
questions.e: PRODIGAL means spending money or resources recklessly; ECONOMICAL means careful not to waste, the opposite. WASTEFUL is a synonym, and PRODIGY (a highly talented young person) and PROLIFIC (producing a lot) are look-alikes.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: IMMACULATE
questions.e: IMMACULATE means perfectly clean and neat; SOILED means made dirty, the opposite. SPOTLESS is a synonym, and IMMATURE (not fully developed) only looks similar.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: JEOPARDY
questions.e: JEOPARDY means danger of loss, harm or failure; SAFETY is freedom from danger, the opposite. DANGER is a synonym, and JEALOUSY and JOURNEY only share the first letter.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: IMPORT
questions.e: To IMPORT is to bring goods into a country from abroad; to EXPORT is to send goods out to another country, the opposite. TRANSPORT and SUPPORT share the root but do not oppose the target.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: MINIMISE
questions.e: To MINIMISE is to reduce something to the smallest possible amount; to MAXIMISE is to make it as large as possible, the opposite. REDUCE is a synonym, and MESMERISE (to fascinate) only rhymes with the target.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: RECALCITRANT
questions.e: RECALCITRANT means stubbornly refusing to obey authority; COMPLIANT means willing to obey and follow rules, the opposite. DEFIANT is a synonym, and RECURRENT (happening repeatedly) only shares the opening letters.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: NEGLIGENT
questions.e: NEGLIGENT means failing to take proper care; CAREFUL is the opposite. CARELESS is a synonym, and NEGLIGIBLE (so small it can be ignored) is a common look-alike trap.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: SUCCESS
questions.e: SUCCESS is the achievement of an aim; FAILURE is the lack of success, the opposite. ACHIEVEMENT is a synonym, and ACCESS and PROCESS only rhyme with the target.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: OBSCURE
questions.e: OBSCURE means not clearly expressed or hard to understand; CLEAR means easy to understand, the opposite. VAGUE is a synonym, and SECURE and ABSURD only sound similar.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: TRANSIENT
questions.e: TRANSIENT means lasting only a short time; ENDURING means lasting for a long time, the opposite. FLEETING is a synonym, and TRANSPARENT (see-through) is a look-alike that has nothing to do with time.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: MODERN
questions.e: MODERN means belonging to the present or recent times; OLD-FASHIONED means belonging to the past and out of date, the opposite. CURRENT is a synonym, and MODERATE and MODEST only share the first letters.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: SOLITARY
questions.e: SOLITARY means alone or preferring to be alone; SOCIABLE means fond of the company of others, the opposite. LONELY is close in meaning to solitary, and SALUTARY (beneficial) and SANITARY (hygienic) are look-alikes.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: SHARP
questions.e: SHARP describes an edge or point that cuts easily; BLUNT describes one that is dull and does not cut well, the opposite. KEEN is a synonym of sharp when describing a blade.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: UNANIMOUS
questions.e: UNANIMOUS means fully in agreement, with everyone voting the same way; DIVIDED means split in opinion, the opposite. UNITED is a synonym, and ANONYMOUS (without a name) is a look-alike trap.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: VOCIFEROUS
questions.e: VOCIFEROUS means loud and forceful in expressing opinions; MUTED means quiet and restrained, the opposite. CLAMOROUS is a synonym, and VORACIOUS (very hungry) only sounds similar.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: ORTHODOX
questions.e: ORTHODOX means following generally accepted beliefs or methods; UNCONVENTIONAL means not following them, the opposite. TRADITIONAL is a synonym, and ORTHOPAEDIC (to do with bones) only shares the first letters.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: BEGINNING
questions.e: The BEGINNING is the point where something starts; the ENDING is where it finishes, the opposite. START is a synonym, and BEGGING only looks like the target.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: DEFICIT
questions.e: A DEFICIT is an amount by which something, such as money, is too small; a SURPLUS is an amount left over, the opposite. SHORTFALL is a synonym, and DEFECT (a fault) only looks similar.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: FEEBLE
questions.e: FEEBLE means lacking physical strength; ROBUST means strong and healthy, the opposite. WEAK is a synonym, and FICKLE (changing loyalties often) only rhymes with the target.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: PROFIT
questions.e: A PROFIT is money gained when income is more than costs; a LOSS is money lost, the opposite. GAIN is a synonym, and PROPHET only sounds like the target.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: ANTIPATHY
questions.e: ANTIPATHY is a strong feeling of dislike; AFFINITY is a natural liking or attraction, the opposite. AVERSION is a synonym, and APATHY (lack of interest) is a look-alike that describes indifference, not liking.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: ANIMOSITY
questions.e: ANIMOSITY is strong dislike or hatred; GOODWILL is a friendly, helpful attitude, the opposite. HOSTILITY is a synonym, and ANONYMITY (being unknown) and ANIMATION only look similar.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: GULLIBLE
questions.e: GULLIBLE means easily deceived and too ready to believe; SCEPTICAL means inclined to doubt claims, the opposite. NAIVE is a synonym, and GALLANT (brave and courteous) only shares the first letter.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: ADMIT
questions.e: To ADMIT is to accept that something is true, often unwillingly; to DENY is to say that it is not true, the opposite. CONFESS is a synonym, and ADMIRE only looks similar.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: ACQUIT
questions.e: To ACQUIT is to declare someone not guilty in court; to CONVICT is to declare someone guilty, the opposite. RELEASE is close in meaning, and ACQUIRE (to obtain) is a look-alike trap.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: CORPULENT
questions.e: CORPULENT means fat, describing a person's body; THIN is the opposite. STOUT is a synonym, and OPULENT (luxurious and rich) only rhymes with the target.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: FERVENT
questions.e: FERVENT means having or showing very strong feeling; APATHETIC means showing no interest or enthusiasm, the opposite. ARDENT is a synonym, and FREQUENT only shares a similar sound.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: PRAISE
questions.e: To PRAISE is to express approval or admiration; to CRITICISE is to point out faults, the opposite. COMMEND is a synonym, and RAISE only rhymes with the target.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: DEBILITATE
questions.e: To DEBILITATE is to make someone or something very weak; to STRENGTHEN is to make it stronger, the opposite. WEAKEN is a synonym, and DELIBERATE (to think carefully) only looks similar.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: ATTRACT
questions.e: To ATTRACT is to pull towards oneself, as a magnet attracts iron; to REPEL is to push away, the opposite. DRAW is a synonym, and ATTACK and ATTAIN only share the first letters.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: PAUCITY
questions.e: PAUCITY means the presence of something in very small amounts; PROFUSION means a very large quantity, the opposite. SCARCITY is a synonym, and PIETY (religious devotion) only rhymes with the target.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: FERTILE
questions.e: FERTILE land can produce good crops; BARREN land produces little or nothing, the opposite. FRUITFUL is a synonym, and FUTILE (useless) is a look-alike trap.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: CONSTRUCTIVE
questions.e: CONSTRUCTIVE means helpful and intended to improve something; DESTRUCTIVE means causing damage or harm, the opposite. HELPFUL is a synonym, and CONSTRICTIVE (tightening) only looks similar.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: EMPHASISE
questions.e: To EMPHASISE is to give special importance to something; to DOWNPLAY is to make it seem less important, the opposite. STRESS is a synonym, and EMPATHISE (to share another's feelings) is a look-alike trap.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: EULOGY
questions.e: A EULOGY is a speech or piece of writing that praises someone highly; a DENUNCIATION is a public condemnation, the opposite. TRIBUTE is a synonym, and ELEGY (a sad poem for the dead) only looks similar.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: TIDY
questions.e: TIDY means arranged neatly and in order; MESSY means untidy and disordered, the opposite. NEAT is a synonym, and TINY and TIDAL only look similar.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: DAWN
questions.e: DAWN is the first light of day; DUSK is the darker stage of twilight at the end of the day, the opposite. DAYBREAK is a synonym, and DOWN only looks similar.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: FLOURISH
questions.e: To FLOURISH is to grow or develop well and healthily; to WITHER is to dry up, weaken and decline, the opposite. THRIVE is a synonym, and FURNISH (to supply furniture) only rhymes with the target.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: ARTIFICIAL
questions.e: ARTIFICIAL means made by people rather than occurring in nature; NATURAL means existing in nature, the opposite. SYNTHETIC is a synonym, and ARTISTIC only shares the first letters.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: HOARD
questions.e: To HOARD is to collect and store away a large supply, often secretly; to SQUANDER is to waste it carelessly, the opposite. STOCKPILE is a synonym, and HORDE (a large crowd) is a sound-alike trap.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: SANGUINE
questions.e: SANGUINE means cheerfully optimistic, especially in a difficult situation; DESPONDENT means having lost hope, the opposite. HOPEFUL is a synonym, and LANGUID (slow and relaxed) only rhymes with the target.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: MOBILE
questions.e: MOBILE means able to move freely or easily; STATIONARY means not moving, the opposite. MOVABLE is a synonym, and NIMBLE (quick and light in movement) is related to motion, not its absence.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: COMPULSORY
questions.e: COMPULSORY means required by a rule or law; OPTIONAL means left to one's own choice, the opposite. MANDATORY is a synonym, and COMPLIMENTARY (given free or expressing praise) only looks similar.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: REFUTE
questions.e: To REFUTE is to prove a statement or theory wrong; to CONFIRM is to show that it is true, the opposite. DISPROVE is a synonym, and REFUSE (to say no to an offer) is a common look-alike trap.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: SENIOR
questions.e: SENIOR means higher in rank or older; JUNIOR means lower in rank or younger, the opposite. ELDER is a synonym, and SENATOR only shares the first letters.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: VOLUNTARY
questions.e: VOLUNTARY means done by free choice; FORCED means done under pressure or compulsion, the opposite. WILLING is a synonym, and VOLATILE (likely to change suddenly) only looks similar.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: FORTHRIGHT
questions.e: FORTHRIGHT means direct and outspoken; EVASIVE means avoiding a direct answer, the opposite. CANDID is a synonym, and FORTUNATE (lucky) only shares the first letters.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: ADVANCE
questions.e: To ADVANCE is to move forward; to RETREAT is to move back or withdraw, the opposite. PROGRESS is a synonym, and ADVICE only looks similar.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: NARROW
questions.e: NARROW means small in width; BROAD means wide from side to side, the opposite. SLENDER is close in meaning, and SHALLOW refers to depth rather than width.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: FAMILIAR
questions.e: FAMILIAR means well known from long experience; STRANGE means unknown or unfamiliar, the opposite. KNOWN is a synonym, and SIMILAR (alike) only rhymes with the target.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: HUMILITY
questions.e: HUMILITY is a modest view of one's own importance; ARROGANCE is an exaggerated sense of one's importance, the opposite. MODESTY is a synonym, and HUMIDITY (moisture in the air) is a look-alike trap.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: ENCOURAGE
questions.e: To ENCOURAGE is to give someone support, confidence or hope; to DISCOURAGE is to take away their confidence, the opposite. INSPIRE is a synonym, and ENCOUNTER (to meet) only shares the first letters.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: PROPONENT
questions.e: A PROPONENT is a person who argues in favour of an idea; an OPPONENT argues against it, the opposite. ADVOCATE is a synonym, and COMPONENT (a part) only rhymes with the target; an EXPONENT is also a supporter or a power in maths, not an opposite.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: EXCLUDE
questions.e: To EXCLUDE is to leave out or keep out; to INCLUDE is to make part of a whole, the opposite. OMIT is a synonym, and EXUDE (to give off) and EXCEED (to go beyond) only look similar.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: INTROVERT
questions.e: An INTROVERT is a shy, quiet person who prefers their own company; an EXTROVERT is outgoing and sociable, the opposite. A LONER is close in meaning, and CONVERT only shares the ending.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: ACCELERATE
questions.e: To ACCELERATE is to increase speed; to DECELERATE is to reduce speed, the opposite. HASTEN is a synonym, and ACCENTUATE (to make more noticeable) only shares the first letters.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: AUSTERE
questions.e: AUSTERE means severely simple and without comfort or decoration; LUXURIOUS means very comfortable and costly, the opposite. SPARTAN is a synonym, and ASTUTE (shrewd) and AUSPICIOUS (promising) are look-alikes.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: CHAOS
questions.e: CHAOS is complete confusion and disorder; ORDER is a neat, organised arrangement, the opposite. DISORDER is a synonym, and CHASM (a deep crack) only looks similar.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: MINOR
questions.e: MINOR means small or less important; MAJOR means large or very important, the opposite. SLIGHT is a synonym, and MINER (a person who digs for coal) only sounds like the target.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: INFLATE
questions.e: To INFLATE is to fill something with air so that it expands; to DEFLATE is to let air out so that it shrinks, the opposite. SWELL is a synonym, and INFLICT (to cause harm) only looks similar.

questions.s: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to: INTREPID
questions.e: INTREPID means fearless and adventurous; COWARDLY means lacking courage, the opposite. FEARLESS is a synonym, and INSIPID (dull, tasteless) only rhymes with the target.

questions.s: CARPENTER : SAW as
questions.e: Bridge: a carpenter uses a saw as a tool of his trade, and a tailor uses a needle as a tool of his. A crop is what a farmer produces, not his tool, and a hospital is a doctor's workplace.

questions.s: PETAL : FLOWER as
questions.e: Bridge: a petal is one part of a flower, and a page is one part of a book. A root grows in soil but is not part of the soil, and water is held in a glass (contents and container), not part of it.

questions.s: HOT : COLD as
questions.e: Bridge: HOT is the opposite of COLD, and TALL is the opposite of SHORT. BIG and LARGE are synonyms, and WARM : HOT shows two degrees of the same quality rather than opposites.

questions.s: DROUGHT : FAMINE as
questions.e: Bridge: a drought can cause a famine, and a virus can cause an infection. FLOOD : RAIN has the order reversed, because rain causes a flood, not the other way round. A doctor brings about a cure as an agent, not as a natural cause.

questions.s: PUPPY : DOG as
questions.e: Bridge: a puppy is a young dog, and a kitten is a young cat. A lamb is a young sheep but wool is its coat, not the adult animal; a den is where a cub lives, and a hen lays an egg.

questions.s: THERMOMETER : TEMPERATURE as
questions.e: Bridge: a thermometer is an instrument that measures temperature, and a barometer is an instrument that measures air pressure. A telescope is used to look at stars but does not measure a quantity, and a stethoscope is a doctor's tool, not something it measures.

questions.s: WHISPER : SHOUT as
questions.e: Bridge: a whisper is a very soft use of the voice and a shout a very loud one, so the pair runs from low to high intensity; a drizzle is light rain and a downpour very heavy rain. LOUD and NOISY are near-synonyms with no change in degree, and SPEAK : LISTEN are two different actions.

questions.s: AUTHOR : BOOK as
questions.e: Bridge: an author creates a book, and a composer creates a symphony. A reader only uses a magazine and does not make it, and a librarian works in a library rather than creating it.

questions.s: SPARROW : BIRD as
questions.e: Bridge: a sparrow is a type of bird, and a rose is a type of flower. FRUIT : MANGO has the order reversed (the category comes first), and a wing is a part of a bird, not a type of one.

questions.s: PILOT : AIRCRAFT as
questions.e: Bridge: a pilot operates an aircraft, and a driver operates a bus. A passenger travels on a train without operating it, and a garage is only a mechanic's workplace.

questions.s: PARSIMONIOUS : GENEROUS as
questions.e: PARSIMONIOUS means extremely unwilling to spend, so it is the opposite of GENEROUS. Bridge: verbose (using too many words) is the opposite of concise. OBSTINATE : STUBBORN and AFFLUENT : WEALTHY are synonym pairs, and something lavish is often expensive, which is not an opposite.

questions.s: SHEEP : FLOCK as
questions.e: Bridge: a sheep is one member of a flock, and a soldier is one member of an army. A nest is a bird's home, not a group of birds, and honey and milk are things bees and cows produce.

questions.s: BOTANY : PLANTS as
questions.e: Bridge: botany is the scientific study of plants, and astronomy is the scientific study of stars and space. A microscope is a tool used in biology and a laboratory is a place where chemistry is done, so neither is the subject studied.

questions.s: BRAKE : STOP as
questions.e: Bridge: a brake is used to stop a vehicle, and a key is used to unlock something; each pair is an object and its function. A pen writes on paper, but paper is the surface, not the action, and a kitchen is only where an oven is kept.

questions.s: HUNGRY : EAT as
questions.e: Bridge: when you are hungry you eat to satisfy the need, and when you are thirsty you drink to satisfy it. Shouting may express anger but does not remove it, and working makes tiredness worse.

questions.s: OASIS : DESERT as
questions.e: Bridge: an oasis is a small isolated area of water and greenery surrounded by desert, as an island is a piece of land surrounded by sea. Sand is the material a dune is made of, and a bridge crosses a river rather than being surrounded by it.

questions.s: FEVER : ILLNESS as
questions.e: Bridge: a fever is a sign that an illness is present, and smoke is a sign that a fire is present. Wax is the material a candle is made from, not a sign of it, and an umbrella is protection against rain.

questions.s: ANCIENT : MODERN as
questions.e: Bridge: ANCIENT is the opposite of MODERN, and VICTORY is the opposite of DEFEAT. BRAVE : COURAGEOUS and OLD : AGED are synonym pairs, so they show sameness, not opposition.

questions.s: IMPECUNIOUS : MONEY as
questions.e: IMPECUNIOUS means having little or no money. Bridge: an impecunious person lacks money, and an ignorant person lacks knowledge. TALENTED : SKILL is the tempting trap, but a talented person has skill rather than lacking it; WEALTHY : PROPERTY is also a having relationship.

questions.s: GRAPE : RAISIN as
questions.e: Bridge: a raisin is a dried grape, and a prune is a dried plum. A seed grows into a tree, which is development, not drying, and an orchard is where apples grow.

questions.s: HELMET : HEAD as
questions.e: Bridge: a helmet is worn to protect the head, and a glove is worn to protect the hand. A ring is also worn on a part of the body, but as an ornament, not for protection.

questions.s: BREAD : BAKER as
questions.e: Bridge: bread is the product made by a baker, and furniture is the product made by a carpenter; the product comes first. CARPENTER : FURNITURE has the right words in the wrong order, and a doctor treats a patient rather than making one.

questions.s: ADORE : LIKE as
questions.e: Bridge: to adore is to like very strongly, and to loathe is to dislike very strongly; the first word is the more intense form of the second. LOVE : HATE are opposites, not two degrees of the same feeling.

questions.s: FRUGAL : WASTE as
questions.e: Bridge: a frugal person avoids waste, and an honest person avoids deceit. PATIENT : WAIT is the closest trap, but a patient person is willing to wait, which is doing the action rather than avoiding it; a brave person has courage.

questions.s: Choose the pair with the same relationship as SEED : TREE
questions.e: Bridge: a seed develops into a tree, and a bud develops into a flower. A branch is part of a full-grown tree, not an earlier stage of it, and a vase only holds a flower.

questions.s: BEE : HIVE as
questions.e: Bridge: a hive is the home in which bees live, and a stable is the shelter in which a horse lives. A pride is a group of lions, not their home, and a calf is a young cow.

questions.s: COBBLER : SHOES as
questions.e: Bridge: a cobbler repairs shoes, and a mechanic repairs cars; each pair is a worker and the thing he mends. Chalk is a teacher's tool and a kitchen is a chef's workplace, so neither is the object repaired.

questions.s: MISER : HOARD as
questions.e: Bridge: a miser is a person who typically hoards money, and a spendthrift is a person who typically squanders it. GLUTTON : STARVE is the trap: a glutton eats too much, so starving is the opposite of his typical action.

questions.s: CUP : TEA as
questions.e: Bridge: a cup is a container that holds tea, and an envelope is a container that holds a letter. A kettle is placed on a stove but does not contain it, and a plate is kept in a kitchen rather than holding it.

questions.s: WOOL : SWEATER as
questions.e: Bridge: wool is the material a sweater is made from, and clay is the material a pot is made from. SHEEP : WOOL shows an animal and what it gives, not a material and the finished product, and a pot only holds soup.

questions.s: CENTIMETRE : LENGTH as
questions.e: Bridge: a centimetre is a unit for measuring length, and a kilogram is a unit for measuring mass. LITRE : WATER is the trap: a litre measures volume, and water is a substance, not a quantity. A ruler and a clock are instruments, not quantities.

questions.s: CANDID : FRANK as
questions.e: Bridge: CANDID means the same as FRANK (open and honest), and LUCID means the same as CLEAR. TIMID : BOLD and DILIGENT : LAZY are opposites, and fragile describes glass rather than meaning the same thing.

questions.s: PHILANTHROPIST : GENEROSITY as
questions.e: Bridge: a philanthropist is a person marked by generosity, and an optimist is a person marked by hopefulness. A pessimist and a novice are marked by the lack of cheerfulness and expertise, and a tyrant demands obedience from others rather than showing it.

questions.s: SPRING : SUMMER as
questions.e: Bridge: summer comes straight after spring, and afternoon comes straight after morning; each pair is in sequence. SUMMER : HOT gives a season and its quality, and WEEK : DAY is a whole and its part.

questions.s: PAINTER : CANVAS as
questions.e: Bridge: a painter works on a canvas as the surface for his work, and a writer writes on paper as the surface for his. FARMER : TRACTOR is the trap: a tractor is a tool or machine, not the surface worked on, and a song is what a singer produces.

questions.s: DOCTOR : HOSPITAL as
questions.e: Bridge: a doctor works in a hospital, and a teacher works in a school; each pair is a worker and the workplace. A recipe is what a chef follows and a verdict is what a judge gives, not places of work.

questions.s: VORACIOUS : HUNGRY as
questions.e: VORACIOUS means extremely hungry. Bridge: voracious is the extreme degree of hungry, as ecstatic is the extreme degree of happy. CONTENT : SATISFIED and TIMID : SHY are near-synonyms of the same strength, and FURIOUS : CALM are opposites.

questions.s: VACCINE : DISEASE as
questions.e: Bridge: a vaccine is used to prevent a disease, and a seat belt is used to prevent injury. FIRE : SMOKE and EXERCISE : SWEAT show cause and effect, the opposite of prevention, and a pharmacy is where medicine is sold.

questions.s: COW : MOO as
questions.e: Bridge: moo is the sound a cow makes, and roar is the sound a lion makes. A tail is a part of a dog and a saddle is equipment for a horse, so neither is a sound.

questions.s: STANZA : POEM as
questions.e: Bridge: a stanza is one section of a poem, and a chapter is one section of a novel. POET : RHYME links a writer with a feature of his work, and a stage is where an actor performs, so neither is a section of a whole.

questions.s: QUENCH : THIRST as
questions.e: Bridge: to quench thirst is to satisfy it completely, and to satiate hunger is to satisfy it completely. PROVOKE : ANGER is the trap: provoking starts anger rather than ending it, and kindling likewise starts a fire.

questions.s: TEACHER : STUDENT as
questions.e: Bridge: a teacher trains and instructs a student, and a coach trains and instructs an athlete. DOCTOR : MEDICINE links a person with something he prescribes, not someone he instructs.

questions.s: ILLITERATE : READ as
questions.e: Bridge: an illiterate person is unable to read, and a mute person is unable to speak. A tall person can reach easily, the opposite of inability, and a tired person needs sleep rather than being unable to do it.

questions.s: ARCHIPELAGO : ISLAND as
questions.e: Bridge: an archipelago is a group of islands, and a constellation is a group of stars. A peninsula is a single piece of land almost surrounded by water, not a group, and a volcano throws out lava.

questions.s: FLOUR : BREAD as
questions.e: Bridge: flour is the main ingredient from which bread is made, and milk is what butter is made from. An oven is the appliance a cake is baked in and a bakery is the shop where bread is sold, so neither is an ingredient.

questions.s: FEATHER : LIGHT as
questions.e: Bridge: a feather is known for being light, and lead is known for being heavy; each pair is a thing and its typical quality. GLASS : WINDOW is a material and a product made from it, not a quality.

questions.s: ERUDITE : SCHOLAR as
questions.e: ERUDITE means having great knowledge. Bridge: a scholar is expected to be erudite, and an acrobat is expected to be agile. TIMID : LION and NOISY : LIBRARY are the opposite of what we expect of a lion and a library.

questions.s: EAR : HEAR as
questions.e: Bridge: the ear is the organ we use to hear, and the nose is the organ we use to smell. EYE : TEAR is the trap: a tear is something the eye produces, while the eye's function is to see.

questions.s: PREFACE : BOOK as
questions.e: Bridge: a preface is an introduction placed at the beginning of a book, and a prologue is an introduction placed at the beginning of a play. EPILOGUE : NOVEL is the trap, because an epilogue comes at the end, not the beginning.

questions.s: TRIM : HAIR as
questions.e: Bridge: you trim hair to cut it shorter, and you mow grass to cut it shorter. Watering a flower helps it grow rather than cutting it, and a brush is the tool used to paint, not the thing acted on.

questions.s: BRUSH : PAINTER as
questions.e: Bridge: a brush is the tool used by a painter, and a scalpel is the tool used by a surgeon; the tool comes first. SURGEON : SCALPEL has the same words in the wrong order, so it does not match the pattern tool : user.

questions.s: FINGER : HAND as
questions.e: Bridge: a finger is a part of the hand, and a toe is a part of the foot. A glove covers the fingers and a sleeve covers the arm, so those pairs are coverings, not body parts within a whole.

questions.s: OBDURATE : YIELD as
questions.e: OBDURATE means stubbornly refusing to change one's mind. Bridge: an obdurate person is unwilling to yield, and a reticent person is unwilling to speak. GARRULOUS : TALK is the trap: a garrulous person talks too much, the opposite of unwillingness, and a credulous person believes too readily.

questions.s: CAMERA : PHOTOGRAPH as
questions.e: Bridge: a camera is the device that produces a photograph, and a loom is the machine that produces cloth. ALBUM : PICTURE is the trap: an album only stores pictures and does not make them, and a lens is a part of a pair of glasses.

questions.s: TORRENT : TRICKLE as
questions.e: Bridge: a torrent is a strong, fast flow of water and a trickle a very weak one, so the pair goes from strong to weak; a gale is a very strong wind and a breeze a light one. RIVER : OCEAN goes the other way, from smaller to larger.

questions.s: KING : PALACE as
questions.e: Bridge: a palace is the home in which a king lives, and a nest is the home in which a bird lives. A pilot flies in the sky but does not live there, and a fin is a part of a fish.

questions.s: REFEREE : MATCH as
questions.e: Bridge: a referee presides over a match and makes sure the rules are followed, and a judge presides over a trial in the same way. A player is a member of a team rather than its official, and a spectator only watches from a stadium.

questions.s: ALLEVIATE : AGGRAVATE as
questions.e: ALLEVIATE means to make a problem less severe and AGGRAVATE means to make it worse, so they are opposites. Bridge: augment (increase) is the opposite of diminish (decrease). MITIGATE : EASE, EXACERBATE : WORSEN and PLACATE : SOOTHE are all synonym pairs.

questions.s: PETROL : CAR as
questions.e: Bridge: petrol is the energy source that powers a car, and electricity is the energy source that powers a fan. A wheel is a part of a bicycle, not its power, and a driver operates a taxi rather than powering it.

questions.s: GENTLE : HARSH as
questions.e: Bridge: GENTLE is the opposite of HARSH, and KIND is the opposite of CRUEL. GENTLE : MILD and HARSH : STRICT reuse words from the stem but are near-synonyms, and soft describes silk.

questions.s: MAP : ATLAS as
questions.e: Bridge: an atlas is a book made up of a collection of maps, and an anthology is a book made up of a collection of poems. A globe is a model of the earth, not one item in a collection, and a compass shows direction.

questions.s: ORCHESTRA : MUSICIAN as
questions.e: Bridge: an orchestra is a group made up of musicians, and a team is a group made up of players; the group comes first. PLAYER : TEAM has the right words in the wrong order, and a band performs a song rather than being made of songs.

questions.s: LACONIC : WORDS as
questions.e: LACONIC means using very few words. Bridge: a laconic person uses few words, and an abstemious person takes little food and drink. VORACIOUS : FOOD is the trap with the opposite meaning, since a voracious eater takes a great deal, and VERBOSE also means using too many words.

questions.s: CAR : GARAGE as
questions.e: Bridge: a car is kept and sheltered in a garage, and an aeroplane is kept and sheltered in a hangar. TRAIN : TRACK is the trap: a train runs on a track but is not stored in it, and a sail is part of a ship.

questions.s: TWENTY : TEN as
questions.e: Bridge: twenty is double ten, and eight is double four. TEN : TWENTY uses the same numbers in the reverse order, giving half instead of double, and five : fifteen is a ratio of three.

questions.s: MEDICINE : ILLNESS as
questions.e: Bridge: a medicine is taken to counter an illness, and an antidote is taken to counter a poison. SNAKE : VENOM is the trap: a snake produces venom rather than countering it, and a bottle only holds pills.

questions.s: PEDAL : BICYCLE as
questions.e: Bridge: a pedal is the part a rider pushes to move a bicycle forward, and an oar is what a rower pushes to move a boat forward. ANCHOR : SHIP is the trap: an anchor holds a ship still instead of moving it.

questions.s: VACUUM : MATTER as
questions.e: Bridge: a vacuum is the complete absence of matter, and darkness is the absence of light. BALLOON : AIR is the opposite, since a balloon is filled with air, and an ocean and a desert are full of water and sand.

questions.s: CACOPHONY : SOUND as
questions.e: CACOPHONY means a harsh, unpleasant mixture of sounds. Bridge: a cacophony is an unpleasant sound, and a stench is an unpleasant smell. FRAGRANCE : SMELL is the trap, but a fragrance is a pleasant smell, and an echo is simply a reflected sound.

questions.s: SYCOPHANT : FLATTER as
questions.e: A SYCOPHANT is a person who praises powerful people too much to gain favour. Bridge: a sycophant typically flatters, and a braggart typically boasts. A hermit avoids company, so socialising is the opposite of what he does, and an orator speaks rather than listens.

questions.s: BOOK : LIBRARY as
questions.e: Bridge: books are kept in a library for the public to use, and paintings are kept in a gallery for the public to see. PAGE : CHAPTER is a part and a whole, and a shelf is made of wood.

questions.s: DRAFT : ESSAY as
questions.e: Bridge: a draft is a rough early version of an essay, and a sketch is a rough early version of a painting. BRUSH : PORTRAIT is the trap: a brush is the tool used to make a portrait, not an earlier version of it.

questions.s: PROTON : POSITIVE as
